package_info.why_malicious: The report does not focus on a specific package, but analyzes the abuse of GitHub as an infrastructure for delivering malware payloads, exfiltrating data, and hosting phishing pages. The maliciousness is at the platform/infrastructure abuse level, not tied to a single package or version.

execution_context.file_location: malicious repository or file hosted on GitHub

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates an HTTP request to download a shell script from a raw.githubusercontent.com URL, pipes the downloaded content directly to the bash shell for execution, resulting in arbitrary remote code execution on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a remote script from an untrusted GitHub repository without validation, a well-known malware delivery technique that enables attackers to run arbitrary code on the victim's machine.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not fetch and execute scripts from arbitrary external sources at runtime without explicit user review or cryptographic verification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some open-source installation scripts use this pattern for convenience, but only from highly trusted sources and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Direct execution of code fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com
Use of shell pipelines to execute remote scripts
Absence of integrity or authenticity checks on downloaded code

execution_context.file_location: malicious repository or file hosted on GitHub

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive data from the victim system, then sends it via an HTTP POST request to the GitHub API, creating or updating an issue in the attacker's repository to covertly exfiltrate the data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code leverages the GitHub API to exfiltrate internal or sensitive data by embedding it in issue creation requests, which is a stealthy method to bypass traditional network security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal code should not transmit sensitive or internal data to external repositories, especially not by abusing issue creation or other covert channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated bug reporting tools may use GitHub issues, but never for exfiltrating confidential or user data.
key_indicators: POST requests to api.github.com/repos/*/issues containing encoded or sensitive data
Use of GitHub API as a data exfiltration channel
Outbound network activity to GitHub API outside of expected development workflows

execution_context.file_location: malicious repository or file hosted on GitHub Pages

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes in the browser of a user visiting a GitHub Pages site, immediately redirecting the user to an external phishing domain, which can result in credential theft or further exploitation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding a forced redirect to a phishing site in a GitHub Pages-hosted script is a common tactic for credential harvesting and user deception.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate GitHub Pages sites should not perform unsolicited redirects to unrelated or malicious domains, especially without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some sites use redirects for legitimate domain migrations, but not to unrelated or known-malicious destinations.
key_indicators: Presence of JavaScript redirect logic in GitHub Pages content
Unsolicited navigation to external, non-affiliated domains
Use of GitHub Pages as a launchpad for phishing attacks

attack_chain.action: Threat actor creates a malicious repository or file on GitHub containing a payload script or redirect logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim accesses or executes code from the malicious repository or visits the compromised GitHub Pages site.

attack_chain.action: Victim system downloads and executes the malicious payload, or the user is redirected to a phishing site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the victim system or credential theft via phishing.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates sensitive data to the attacker's GitHub repository using the GitHub API.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data via GitHub issues or other repository features.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of code fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com or similar GitHub raw URLs at runtime
Outbound HTTP POST requests to api.github.com/repos/*/issues containing encoded or sensitive data
Presence of JavaScript redirect logic in HTML/JS files hosted on GitHub Pages that point to external domains
file_indicators: Shell scripts or binaries downloaded from raw.githubusercontent.com within installation or runtime scripts
References to raw.githubusercontent.com URLs in executable scripts
HTML or JavaScript files on GitHub Pages containing window.location or similar redirect statements
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS connections to raw.githubusercontent.com for script or binary downloads
POST requests to api.github.com/repos/*/issues with data payloads indicative of exfiltration
Browser traffic from GitHub Pages sites to known phishing or malicious domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for scripts or binaries being downloaded and executed from raw.githubusercontent.com or other GitHub raw URLs at runtime. Inspect network traffic for unusual POST requests to api.github.com/repos/*/issues, especially those containing encoded or sensitive data. Scan HTML/JS files on GitHub Pages for redirect logic that points to external domains. Correlate these behaviors with repository trust levels and user activity to identify suspicious or unauthorized use of GitHub as a malware delivery or exfiltration platform.
